_README: Post-level corrections keyed by the post's own URL -- tools/harvest.py. Hand input, which is why this is committed. Two kinds, and both are things no derivation can reach: a post that names the wrong level (`coll`/`level` retarget it, `image_level` says the filenames carry a different number than the title and the title is the one to believe), and a screenshot cell that carries no information for any eye or table to read. `frames` holds the latter, per goal frame, in the game's own A-P/1-16 coordinates: `cells` for the PF symbol under an occluding sprite, `tank` for a frame that lost the tank entirely. Keep `frames` minimal -- the tank's own position and facing are derivable from the pixels even where the PF is not (sprites.facings()), so a `tank` entry is only for a frame that shows no tank at all. Every entry is checked by playing the level and the note records the check, plus whatever the .lvl independently corroborates.

https://lasertanksolutions.blogspot.com/.note: Titled 'KaserTank - 826', a collection the corpus does not ship. The images are LaserTank_826.png and LaserTank_826b.png, LaserTank.lvl 826 is named 'siguiendo el camino' which is the post's own title exactly, and LaserTank 826 has no other post. Confirmed by Michal, session 39.

Title and level are right -- Sokoban-I.lvl 344 is 'Symmetric 24'. The two images are misnamed SokobanI_343_H3.png and SokobanI_343_I14.png, and they are per-flag frames that Sokoban-I 343's own post does not carry, so they are not duplicates of it. The post has no start screenshot. Confirmed by Michal, session 39: played it, the level is 344.

b.note: The frame decodes with 0 unknown cells and no tank anywhere in it -- the source image is wrong, not the decode: B11 shows the bare 'D' terrain the tank should be standing on. Michal played the level, session 39: at that board the tank is at B11 facing right.

I2 is the tank standing on an anti-tank, which occludes the cell completely: '<' (PF 10) and '#' (PF 4, a wreck) draw identical pixels and so does any background under them, so sprites.py drops the tile and no eye can read it either. Michal, session 39: the tank is looking up on an anti-tank that started at J2. The .lvl corroborates the facing -- J2 is '<' -- so the anti-tank was pushed one west and kept facing left. The tank itself needs no entry: the facing is derivable from the pixels.

Same cell shape as LaserTank 899: the tank on an anti-tank, PF unreadable from the pixels. Michal, session 39: the tank stands on an anti-tank that started at E15. The .lvl corroborates -- E15 is '<' -- so it was pushed one west facing left. The pixels put the tank at D15 facing down, derivably, so only the PF underneath is hand input.

A7 is a torn tunnel blit: the flat ColorList[1] green rectangle with its GDI pen outline and sprite 55 never drawn over it, which hides whatever stood on the cell -- 484 green pixels and 92 black, nothing else. Michal, session 39: anti-tank facing right on a green mirror, on both A7 and B7; B7 draws cleanly and decodes on its own. The PF the solver wants is the anti-tank, so '>'.
